narration.text: Yield to an emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights from any direction by moving right and stopping without obstructing an intersection. After the emergency vehicle passes, signal before reentering the roadway and do so only when safe. Keep at least five hundred feet behind a fire truck using warning lights or a siren, and do not drive or park in the block where it has stopped for a fire alarm. At a highway emergency, traffic stop or stopped vehicle displaying warnings, reduce speed and provide a wide berth when practical without endangering opposing traffic. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

lines.text: When traffic allows it safely, move into a lane away from the incident or emergency
personnel and promptly leave a lane that is wholly or partly blocked.

narration.text: When traffic allows it safely, move into a lane away from the incident or emergency personnel and promptly leave a lane that is wholly or partly blocked. Follow authorized traffic directions and emergency signals around a crash, fire, maintenance activity or other roadway emergency. A move-over-law violation brings a fine and penalty assessment, with a larger fine for another offense within twelve months. For a police traffic stop, pull aside, stop fully and select park; stay inside unless the officer requests that you leave. Switch off the engine, activate hazard lamps and, at night, illuminate the interior during the described police stop. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

Watch orange work-zone signs, cones, barrels, large vehicles and workers, and reduce speed even without a newly posted lower limit. Increase following space in a work zone, monitor surrounding traffic and remain ready to stop. Use exceptional caution at night in a work zone even when no workers are visible.
